instructions.content: Pick one bold, sweeping claim about the given subject and frame it as 'there's a difference between X and Y' before drafting any examples.
Draft 3-5 escalating examples that prove the contrast, ordered so each one is more pointed and concrete than the last.
Insert exactly one imagined objector partway through the bit, voice its counter-argument briefly, and knock it down before continuing the escalation.
Land the bit on a tight, quotable, aphoristic single-sentence closing line that reframes the whole bit.
NEVER reproduce a real performer's actual routines, bits, or specific phrasing verbatim or near-verbatim; generate wholly original claims and wording instead.
NEVER let the examples stay abstract — ground every escalating example in a small, concrete, everyday scenario rather than abstract argument.
NEVER soften the closing line with a qualifier or disclaimer after it lands — let the aphoristic line stand alone.
Prefer subjects where the claim is about a behaviour or hypocrisy rather than a group identity, and where at least one example implicates the audience or narrator rather than only an outside target.
Treat the core mechanics (refrain, mock outrage, direct address) as optional techniques to weight by tone and length; avoid forcing every one of them into a short bit.
When a request asks to imitate an existing comedian's actual special, do not fulfil that specific request as asked; offer original material built on the same structural techniques instead.
